title: The Manipura chakra in the destiny matrix: fire at the very centre of the chart

seo.title: Manipura chakra in the destiny matrix: calculation and 16 combinations
seo.description: Manipura chakra in the destiny matrix is calculated from the centre. Find yours by date of birth in a minute and see what 10 / 10 / 20 and 15 other rows mean.

short: Manipura is the third chakra, the chakra of fire. In the destiny matrix its theme is will and independence. Its three numbers answer three questions: how you take on a task, what keeps you going, and how you live through the outcome — success, rejection, other people’s judgement. All three numbers come from a single point, the centre of the matrix. That is why the first two numbers in the row are always the same and the third is their sum: 4 / 4 / 8, 7 / 7 / 14, 10 / 10 / 20. There are only 16 such rows, and every one of them is covered below. To find yours, add up three numbers from your date of birth and look the sum up in the table.

sections.h2: Find your Manipura in a minute
paragraphs: You need three numbers from your date of birth. One rule runs through the whole calculation: if a number is greater than 22, add up its digits.

ol: **Day arcanum (A).** Your day of birth. If it is greater than 22, add up its digits: 24 → 6, 31 → 4.
**Month (B).** The number of the month, from 1 to 12.
**Year arcanum (C).** Add up the digits of the year. If the result is greater than 22, add them up again: 1985 → 23 → 5, 1990 → 19.
**Add A + B + C** and find the sum in the table.

paragraphs: Take 24 March 1985: 6 + 3 + 5 = **14**. The sum 14 sits in the row **10 / 10 / 20**.

paragraphs: The table is complete. For any date of birth the sum A + B + C falls between 4 and 56, and every one of those numbers is in the table.

If you would rather check it against the formula: first comes the bottom point of the matrix, D = A + B + C, reduced. Then the centre, E = A + B + C + D, reduced as well. For 24.03.1985: D = 14, E = 6 + 3 + 5 + 14 = 28 → 10. Physics and energy are 10, emotions are 10 + 10 = 20.
If you already know the centre of your matrix (point E, also called the comfort zone), you already have your Manipura: E / E / E + E.

sections.h2: What Manipura is: the city of jewels and the chakra of fire
paragraphs: The name is Sanskrit: mani means jewel, pura means city. In the Indian tradition it is the third of the seven chakras, counting from the bottom, and its element is fire. The fullest description comes from Purnananda’s treatise Shat-chakra-nirupana (1577), which Arthur Avalon (John Woodroffe) translated into English in The Serpent Power (1919). According to the treatise, Manipura lies at the root of the navel. It is a lotus of ten petals, the colour of heavy rain clouds. Inside it is a triangular region of fire that shines like the rising sun. There Vahni, the god of fire, sits on a ram, and his seed syllable is “Ram”. The solar plexus and the colour yellow came later, from modern Western charts that paint the seven chakras in the colours of the rainbow.

In her textbook Holistic Tarot, Benebell Wen gives this chakra a position in the Seven Chakras Spread. She reads the card in that position for career issues, level of achievement and persistence. The chakra, she writes, **“relates to the ego, personal power, the wheel of force, and how much drive the Seeker possesses for success in his or her career”**. The Sanskrit word chakra itself means “wheel”.
In the destiny matrix Manipura covers more than a career: its theme is **will and independence**. Manipura answers these questions:

ul: which tasks you take on gladly and which only by forcing yourself;
how you act when the decision is yours;
what keeps you from giving up: growth, order, the thrill, the truth, freedom;
what happens inside you when the result arrives: praise, rejection, failure, uncertainty;
where independence turns into control, haste or dodging the conversation.

paragraphs: What Manipura does not show: the size of your income, your job title or the state of your digestion. Its numbers describe how you act, not how much you have already achieved.

sections.h2: Where Manipura sits in the destiny matrix: right in the centre
paragraphs: The destiny matrix is an eight-pointed star made of two squares. The personal square has four points: the day arcanum (A) on the left, the month (B) at the top, the year (C) on the right and their sum (D) at the bottom. In the middle of the star stands point E, the sum of all four. On the site it is labelled the centre of the chart: the baseline state a person returns to after any strain.

Every other chakra takes two different points. Sahasrara takes the day and the month, Muladhara the year and the bottom point, and the rest take inner points between the edge of the star and the centre. Manipura takes one point twice: both physics and energy are the centre. That is why its row always looks like “X / X / X + X”.

Yet the centre does not stay in its own row. All the inner points are counted from it: J = A + E, K = B + E, L = C + E, M = D + E. This is how the Manipura number finds its way into the calculation of four more chakras. Here is what that looks like for 24.03.1985, where the centre is 10:

paragraphs: Anahata even takes the centre twice: first through Vishuddha, then once more directly.

The anatomical solar plexus is a knot of nerves from which branches run out to the organs of the abdomen. Manipura in the matrix works in a similar way: from the centre, numbers run out into five rows of the table. It is only an image, but an easy one to remember.

None of this makes Manipura more important than the other chakras: each row is read on its own. But it does lead to something worth knowing. If you and a friend share the same Manipura, your other six rows are almost certainly different. The centre is shared, but the day, the month and the year belong to each of you alone.

sections.h2: Why the first two numbers match — and why that is not a mistake
paragraphs: Someone sees 7 / 7 / 14 in the row and decides either that the calculator is broken or that they have a “double Chariot”, and so twice the drive. Neither is true. Here one arcanum answers two different questions.

ul: **Physics — how you act.** How you take on a task, plan, negotiate and carry the work through to a result.
**Energy — what gives you strength.** Why you get involved at all, and what helps you not to give up halfway.
**Emotions — how you live through the result.** Success, rejection, judgement, uncertainty. This number is the sum of the first two, but it is read as a separate question.

paragraphs: Take 7 / 7 / 14. In physics The Chariot means driving the work towards a finishing line: choosing a direction and keeping different forces in one harness. In energy the same Chariot becomes fuel: strength comes from the movement itself, from each stretch of road left behind. In the first case it is the reins; in the second, the joy of the road. Temperance in emotions adds a sense of measure: success does not go to your head, and a rejection does not sting for long.

In other chakras physics and energy are set by two different arcana, and there can be tension between them: you do one thing, but your strength comes from another. In Manipura one arcanum answers both questions, so method and motive speak the same language. The most surprising thing in this row is the third number. It shows what happens to you when the work meets its result.
And that third number cannot be read from a dictionary. Justice stands in emotions in three different Manipuras, and in the full reading each has its own caption:

head: Manipura
Caption for Justice in emotions
What it is about
rows: being glad of an assessment when it is deserved, and accepting a rejection when it comes with a reason
leaving once the obligations are met and the reason has been named
after a bold attempt, counting honestly what paid off and whom you owe

paragraphs: The card shows a woman with a sword and scales, and Waite sees in her **“the moral principle which deals unto every man according to his works”**. It is one card, but it weighs different things: next to The Emperor, the assessment of your contribution; next to Death, the debts left over when something ends; next to The Fool, the price of a bold leap. The pairs 3 / 3 / 6 and 12 / 12 / 6, with The Lovers in emotions, work the same way, and so do 5 / 5 / 10 and 14 / 14 / 10, with The Wheel of Fortune.

sections.h2: Which numbers Manipura can hold, and which it never does
paragraphs: There are only 16 rows, and they turn up at very different rates. Below is the share of each among all dates of birth since 1900:
Manipura depends only on the sum A + B + C, so people born on different days, in different months and years can share a row. If yours is one of the common ones, roughly one date in nine has it too.

**Six arcana never appear in Manipura at all:** The Magician (1), The High Priestess (2), The Devil (15), The Star (17), The Sun (19) and The World (21). They do not turn up in any of the three columns for any date. The reason lies in how the centre is built. It is made of the sum A + B + C plus the same sum again, only reduced, so in effect the sum is doubled. Numbers from 14 upwards come almost only from small sums. Doubling them needs no reduction, so the result is even. The odd numbers 15, 17, 19 and 21 never land in the centre, and 1 and 2 cannot come out either directly or after reduction.

A curious coincidence: the treatise compares Manipura’s fire to the rising sun, popular charts place it at the solar plexus, and yet The Sun never lands in this chakra. There is no point looking for meaning in this: it is arithmetic, not symbolism.

**The rarest Manipura is 16 / 16 / 5.** Between 1900 and 1999 it went only to people born on 1 or 2 January or on 1 February, and not in every year: just 17 dates in the whole century. For dates in the 2000s the rare rows come up almost three times as often as across the 20th century as a whole: 4.2% of dates against about one and a half per cent. A year like 2000 or 2003 gives a small number, so the sum of the date comes out small too.

Find your row. **Physics** is how you act, **energy** is what gives you strength, **emotions** is how you live through the result. Below, all 16 Manipura interpretations from our full reading are open: three cards with captions and the whole story of the combination. They are possible scenarios to recognise yourself in, not a verdict.

sections.h2: Manipura 10 / 10 / 20 in the destiny matrix: The Wheel of Fortune and Judgement
paragraphs: This is one of the most common rows: about 11% of dates of birth. It comes up when A + B + C equals 5, 14, 23, 32, 41 or 50 — for example, for people born on 24.03.1985, 17.11.1975 or 11.04.1997.

**Physics and energy: 10, The Wheel of Fortune.** Waite describes the wheel as the perpetual motion of the universe and the flux of human life. The Sphinx on it stands for equilibrium, or, in Waite’s words, **“stability amidst movement”**. Behind the symbol Waite sees **“the denial of chance”**, so this is not a card of blind luck. In physics the Wheel shows how you act: you notice that circumstances have turned, rework the plan and catch the moment. In energy it becomes fuel. Your strength grows once the work starts moving, and sameness, where nothing changes, drains it.

**Emotions: 20, Judgement.** An angel sounds the trumpet and people rise from their tombs. Waite reads the scene as a transformation in answer to a summons, **“which summons is heard and answered from within”**, and asks: **“What is that within us which does sound a trumpet and all that is lower in our nature rises in response?”** This is how the result is felt in Manipura. Success or failure sounds like a signal that a stage is complete and it is time to move on to the next. Judgement here is neither punishment nor a sentence. It is the moment when it becomes clear where to go next. Judgement in the emotions of Manipura appears in this row only.

The arcanum’s role changes everything. In the rows 5 / 5 / 10 and 14 / 14 / 10 the Wheel stands in emotions: the turn happens to you, and you live through it. In 10 / 10 / 20 the Wheel stands in physics and energy: the turn is what you act with and what fires you up.

But Manipura is one row out of seven. The same person born on 24.03.1985 has Anahata 8 / 5 / 13, Vishuddha 16 / 13 / 11 and Svadhisthana 15 / 6 / 21. In the full reading each of these rows is read separately, with a text of its own. None of them can be found from the sum of three numbers the way Manipura can.

Popular descriptions call Manipura the chakra of money, status and power. Wen uses it to look at career, achievement and persistence. In the destiny matrix Manipura shows how you work and how you live through the result, not how much you earn. **It is the chakra of the work, not of the wallet.**

What ties it to money is the work itself. The row 8 / 8 / 16 is about how you negotiate shares and terms. The row 4 / 4 / 8 says that you need authority, not just tasks. The row 9 / 9 / 18 is about finished work that stays out of sight for a long time while it is unclear how it will be judged. All of this affects what you earn, even though it names no sums.

There is a direct arithmetical link too. The entry of the money line is point L = year + centre, and the entry of relationships is point M = bottom point + centre. These are the same two numbers that stand in Svadhisthana. For 24.03.1985: L = 5 + 10 = 15, M = 14 + 10 = 24 → 6. The Manipura number goes into the sum for both the money entry and the relationship entry. But money is read along its own line: the entry, the direction, the crossing of the channels. Manipura alone is not enough for that.

ul: **The numbers name arcana; they are not scores.** 22 is not stronger than 3, and a rare row does not mean a special destiny. There is no such thing as an empty Manipura: everyone has three cards in it.
**Matching numbers do not mean imbalance.** Physics and energy coincide because of how the calculation works, and that is true for everyone. It shows neither an excess of fire nor a block.

**“Plus” and “minus” are not two different arcana but two modes of one.** The part of each reading above about where things go off track grows out of the same strength that is described in physics and energy. Instead of asking “how do I unblock my Manipura?”, it is more useful to ask: where does my way of acting go too far?
**Manipura says nothing about your physical condition.** Neither the digestive organs nor the “solar plexus” in the medical sense can be read from the numbers.

paragraphs: Seven chakras, three arcana in each: physics, energy, emotions. Manipura is row 03, and its first two numbers are always the same. The numbers and cards appear as soon as you run the calculation. The interpretation of each row opens in the full reading; until you pay, the row shows a lock.

All 16 Manipura interpretations are already open in this article. After the free calculation you will see your whole chakra table: seven rows, 21 arcana, numbers and cards. The full reading adds the interpretations of the other six chakras for your date and an overall conclusion on the chart. Every row is read the same way as Manipura is here:

ul: a heading that names the essence of your combination;
a caption for each of the three cards: the role it plays in this particular row;
three paragraphs: the theme of the chakra and what each arcanum brings to it, the whole picture in everyday life, and the point where strength starts to get in the way.

paragraphs: The texts are not assembled from a dictionary. Every combination has a text written for it alone, 1,908 in the section in all. Manipura has 16, one for each possible row. The other chakras have far more combinations: Anahata 393, Muladhara 383, Vishuddha 380, Ajna 336, Sahasrara 264, Svadhisthana 136.

sections.h2: What this article is based on

ul: **Calculation** — the classic destiny matrix with points A–T: D = A + B + C, centre E = A + B + C + D. Manipura = E, E and their sum. Sums greater than 22 are reduced by adding up their digits. The frequencies, rare rows and impossible arcana were counted by going through all 46,297 dates from 1 January 1900 to 3 October 2026.
**Tradition** — Purnananda’s Shat-chakra-nirupana (1577) in the translation by Arthur Avalon (John Woodroffe), The Serpent Power (1919).

**Card meanings** — A. E. Waite, The Pictorial Key to the Tarot (1910, reissued 1922). The quotations are given in Waite’s original wording. Manipura’s theme in the Seven Chakras Spread comes from Benebell Wen, Holistic Tarot (2015), chapter 14.

**The meaning of the arcana by column and the reading of each row** — the author’s interpretation. Neither Waite nor Wen wrote about the destiny matrix or about the physics / energy / emotions columns.
The destiny matrix is an esoteric model for self-reflection, with no scientific evidence behind it. It is not a forecast, and it is not financial, career or medical advice.

paragraphs: **Find out what feeds your fire.** Enter your date of birth and you will see your Manipura straight away, along with the other six chakras — 21 arcana in all. In the full reading every chakra is read in full: how you act, what gives you strength and where that strength starts to get in the way.

intro: Three facts set Manipura apart from the other six chakras:

ul: **it is calculated from a single point.** Physics and energy are both the centre of the matrix, so the numbers always come in a pair;
**its number runs through five of the seven chakras.** Svadhisthana, Anahata, Vishuddha and Ajna are counted from the centre too; only Muladhara and Sahasrara do without it;
**there are only 16 variants.** The Magician, The High Priestess, The Devil, The Star, The Sun and The World never appear in Manipura, whatever the date of birth.

intro: Manipura and the other six chakras appear as soon as you run the calculation. Free, and no sign-up needed.

faq.q: How do I calculate Manipura in the destiny matrix?
faq.a: Add up the day arcanum, the month and the year arcanum (numbers above 22 are reduced by adding up their digits) and find the sum in the table above. Or work out the centre of the matrix: E = A + B + C + D. Manipura is E / E / E + E. Example: 24.03.1985 → 6 + 3 + 5 = 14 → 10 / 10 / 20.

The Wheel of Fortune in physics and energy: you act in rhythm with change, and your strength grows once things start moving. Judgement in emotions: the result feels like a signal that a stage is complete and it is time for the next. The weak spot is a lull, when you want to wait for a sign instead of taking ordinary steps. More in the section on 10 / 10 / 20 above.

faq.q: Why are the first two numbers in Manipura the same?
faq.a: Because both columns take the same point — the centre of the matrix, E. It is a feature of the calculation, not a mistake and not “double strength”. In physics the arcanum is read as a way of acting, in energy as a source of strength.

faq.q: Where is Manipura in the destiny matrix?
faq.a: In the centre of the matrix, at point E. In our chakra table it is row 03: we start from Muladhara and come to Manipura through Svadhisthana.

It is more the chakra of work. It shows how you take on a job, negotiate and live through the result, but not the size of your income. The centre goes into the sum for the entry of the money line (L = year + centre), but money itself is read along its own line.

faq.q: How can I tell if my Manipura is blocked or weak?
faq.a: Not from the numbers. Arcanum numbers are not scores, and there is no such thing as an empty Manipura. It is more useful to look at where your way of acting goes too far: every row above describes this in its part about where things go off track.

faq.q: Why do The Sun, The Devil and The World never appear in Manipura?
faq.a: The centre of the matrix is in effect a doubled sum of the date, so the large numbers in it are always even. 15, 17, 19 and 21 do not come up for any date of birth, and neither do 1 and 2. In all, 16 rows are possible in Manipura.

faq.q: Why does another calculator show different numbers?
faq.a: Most often it comes down to reduction. Here the digits are added up: 12 + 12 = 24 → 2 + 4 = 6. If you subtract 22 instead, you get 2, and the row 12 / 12 / 6 turns into 12 / 12 / 2. The same goes for the year: 1999 → 28 → 10 here, and 6 by subtraction. If the numbers do not match, check the reduction rule first and the interpretations second.

faq.q: Is Manipura different for men and women?
faq.a: No. Gender plays no part in the calculation, so a man and a woman with the same date of birth have the same numbers.

The destiny matrix uses the old Marseille numbering: 8 is Justice, 11 is Strength. In Waite’s deck and in many Tarot books these two cards are swapped. So an interpretation is checked by the card’s name, not by its number: the meaning rests on the name.
